chapter: Blues, American music and musicians' backgrounds
title: Democratized recording and the lowering bar
summary: He thinks laptop recording is democratized but sounds like it, and that earlier players had to be great to work.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: least this is the way it used to be. Now, somebody told me today, one of the students said something to me about — I was talking about the recording and how it used to be, the studios. A student said, “Yeah but it might be more democratized now because everybody can make a record.” And I said, “You’re right. Everybody who has a laptop can put on garage band and make a record. But — it is democratized, but I said, “To me, to my ears, in my experience, it sounds like somebody sitting down with their computer making a record. It’s not the same. We all were into high fidelity. George Massenburg was talking — “I want the records to be hi fi.” We wanted our stuff to sound hi fi. Our instruments, the records that I was producing them, it was like we wanted to be there. And now, I keep talking about this. Caroline, my wife, hears this all the time about the bar keeps getting lower and lower and lower. Now that’s an old guy talking, in retrosp — you know I don’t want to be one of the old guys talking about well in my day — but you know once you had to be, to do what we did you had to be great as a player or as a producer or as a songwriter or as an engineer. Or you didn’t get work the next week.
